metadata.title: A four-parameter family of reversible three-species mass-action continua without a common factor
metadata.description:
Version 2 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21753997

We determine an exact four-dimensional rate family on one fixed reversible, one-linkage, three-species mass-action support with ten complexes and ten reversible pairs. Every positive member has full stoichiometric rank and vanishes on the same compact positive algebraic ellipse. The positive rate set is a rational relatively open polyhedral cone, while a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the family has geometrically coprime coordinate polynomials.

A primitive positive integer specialization has largest rate 10296 and rate sum 52464, simultaneously optimal for both objectives within the fixed support and conic-preserving integral family. Exact certificates also give radical decompositions for both displayed specializations and a transverse-stability classification for the immutable Version 1 ellipse.

  • fixed support: three species, ten complexes, ten reversible pairs, one linkage class;
  • conic-remainder matrix: 21 x 20, rank 16, nullity 4;
  • coordinate gcd: geometrically one on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the constrained family;
  • verification: four exact replay layers, including a separately implemented v2 audit.

The continuum-preserving family has codimension sixteen in the ambient twenty-dimensional rate space. This is not a claim of persistence under arbitrary rate perturbations or global minimality of the ten-complex support.

Scoped PDFs, exact source, verifier archives, checksums, and one-command reproduction instructions are attached to the GitHub Version 2 release. The automatic archive here is the tagged monorepo source.

DOI scope. Zenodo repository-level concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21753404 groups unrelated releases from the AlecKriebel/Math monorepo and is not a paper-specific all-versions DOI. Cite this version using 10.5281/zenodo.21753997.

Priority scope. Boros, Craciun, and Yu already supplied a positive-dimensional fixed-support same-curve rate family, but every member retains a common scalar factor. A targeted primary-source audit through 1 August 2026 found no earlier weakly reversible fixed-support positive family preserving a compatibility-class continuum while being generically free of a coordinate common factor within that family. This is a conservative, nonexhaustive audit conclusion. The release is unreviewed; a DOI is not a correctness certificate.
